title: Reduce idle UI polling
summary: Reduced EVE local UI idle CPU usage by replacing aggressive 5-second background polling for expensive config, snapshot, repository, and plan history queries with foreground-only refresh policies. Pending approval checks remain fast but centralized through the query client policy.
userVisibleChange: When the EVE UI is open or in a background browser tab, it performs substantially fewer repeated filesystem and Git-backed API refreshes while still refreshing visible data on focus and reconnect.

risks.title: Freshness is slower while staying on an idle foreground page
risks.mitigation: The UI still refreshes resources every 30 seconds, refreshes plan history every 10 seconds, and refetches on window focus and reconnect.

timeline.title: Identified aggressive live query policy
timeline.summary: The UI marked snapshots, repositories, repository details, and plan requests as 5-second background polling queries.

timeline.title: Centralized and reduced refresh intervals
timeline.summary: Changed resource queries to 30-second foreground-only refreshes, plan history to 10-second foreground-only refreshes, and kept pending approval polling at a centralized 2-second foreground-only interval.

timeline.title: Verified Go and UI behavior
timeline.summary: Ran focused and broad Go/UI tests plus the production UI build.

decisions.title: Throttle expensive resource queries to foreground refreshes
decisions.rationale: Snapshot, repository, and config endpoints can scan .eve state and invoke Git commands, so polling them every five seconds in background tabs creates avoidable CPU load.

decisions.title: Keep pending approval checks short but foreground-only
decisions.rationale: Approval workflows need responsive updates, but they do not require hidden tabs to continue polling in the background.

validation.output: tsc --noEmit && vite build && node scripts/copy-dist.mjs completed successfully
